Role Title: Mechanical Design Engineer — Aerospace CNC Parts
Role Type: Contractor
Location: Fully remote
Opportunity Snapshot
Pay: $90 - $155/hour
Engagement: Project-based, hourly tracked per task
Location: Fully remote, no geographic restrictions
You'll need: 5+ years designing CNC-machined production parts, with technical decision authority, and access to parametric CAD software
Your tasks: Author original CAD part packages, and peer review packages from other engineers
Your engineering judgment is what matters here — no prior AI experience required.
Each package is a new part you design from scratch: a difficult, high-value CNC part with a specific machining challenge, backed by a drawing with full GD&T, a design rationale, and a production scenario you justify from experience. Every part is independently reviewed by three other engineers, and you'll review others' work as well.
What you'll do

• Design original parts in parametric CAD, delivered as native files plus STEP.

• Produce the technical drawing: dimensions, tolerances, GD&T and datums, material and condition, finish, revision, drawing standard.

• Write the design context: intended function, interfaces, operating conditions, the machining challenge, and your material and process rationale.

• Build the production scenario: estimated unit cost and drivers, CNC cycle and setup hours, assumed volume, sourcing difficulty and lead time — with the engineering basis for each estimate.

• Peer review other engineers' packages against technical quality, production realism, and engineering value, with part-specific evidence for every score.

• Revise your own packages against review findings.

What we're looking for

• 5+ years of production engineering experience with comparable CNC parts, materials and processes in aerospace or space hardware.

• 
Technical decision authority: you owned or approved critical design choices — drawing, tolerance or material approval, production release, or enforcing engineering quality standards. Design leads, principal and staff engineers, and technical authorities are the profile.

• Experience at OEMs or suppliers whose engineering standards you can reproduce.

• Strong GD&T and tolerancing judgment, including cost and inspection implications.

• Access to parametric CAD software (SolidWorks, NX, CATIA, Creo or similar) and the ability to deliver native files plus STEP.

• Industry experience, not academic.

How the selection process works

• Apply and complete the screening questions

• Complete the AI interview for this role — it's how your expertise gets in front of the client

• Profile review, including evidence of comparable parts and decisions owned

• Onboarding — our Talent Ops team will get you set up

Meet Siena
Siena is the Agent of Record for CX, built for consumer brands like Spanx, FIGS, Brooklinen, and Grüns.
It runs as a connected multi-agent stack on top of a shared intelligence layer: agents that sell, support, listen, handle social and voice across the entire customer journey, turning every conversation into signal you can act on.

The team
We are a small, fully distributed, global team. We have built leverage into how we work, which is what lets a team this size move at the speed we do.
We hire athletes. Everyone here owns real outcomes, defaults to writing over meetings, communicates with directness, and acts the moment they see something worth acting on. Low ego, high standards, fast clock.
If you want to set the bar rather than follow one, keep reading.
The Role
Siena runs customer experience for consumer brands through a connected multi-agent stack. As Product Manager, Core Agent Platform, you'll own the platform those agents run on, from its current capabilities to where it goes next. You'll own how we measure, test and improve agent performance, and how customers see it. You'll work directly with engineering, deployment and customers, and you'll be expected to build as well as specify.
What You'll Do
• 
Own the core agent platform end to end, including the roadmap and the day-to-day product decisions.
• 
Build and ship the evaluation, testing and monitoring systems that make agent performance measurably better over time.
• 
Design and run structured experiments and A/B tests across agent workflows.
• 
Give customers clear visibility into how their agents are performing.
• 
Prototype your own ideas with coding agents, and ship them where you can, rather than waiting on a hand-off.
• 
Work with customers and our deployment team to understand what's working in the field and turn it into product.
Who You Are
The Bar: If you're missing any of these, this isn't the role for you.
• 
3+ years as a PM in CX, ecommerce, helpdesk or AI automation.
• 
Technical fluency: you can explain how webhooks, OAuth and integrations work and have made product decisions around them.
• 
AI-native builder: you use tools like Claude, Cursor or v0 daily and have prototyped your own product ideas with them.
Strong Signal: Not dealbreakers, but what separates a good hire from a great one.
• 
You've run structured experiments or A/B tests and can say what the data did and didn't tell you.
• 
You've built dashboards or visibility features people actually relied on.
• 
You're confident with customers: you've sat in on calls, run demos, and know what end users really complain about.
• 
You act like the CEO of your product area: strong opinions, and a habit of building and talking to customers without being asked.
Nice to Have: Bonus, not required.
• 
Engineering background, or you've shipped production code yourself.
Not a Fit If:
• 
You wait to be told what to build.
• 
You want a narrowly scoped PM seat with a fixed roadmap handed to you.
• 
You're not comfortable being customer-facing or getting on a call to demo your own work.
• 
You'd rather stay behind the product than own the messy, ambiguous parts.
• 
You need a designer or engineer to turn your product vision into something people can click.
Why Siena?
Real ownership. You will own problems, not tasks, with the autonomy to solve them your way and the trust to do it without a manager in your inbox.
Work that ships and matters. What you build reaches real consumer brands fast.
A category we are creating. The Agent of Record is new ground, with unsolved problems and cutting-edge models, not a crowded field to compete in.
A team that respects your judgment. Globally distributed, async-first, low bureaucracy. We hire adults and treat you like one.
Great salary plus equity or stock grants. Own a piece of what you build.
Learning budget. If you are growing, so are we.
AI-fluency by default. Few places will push your work with production AI further or faster.
Our values
The people who thrive here are curious, customer-obsessed, and take ownership without being asked. They fix problems first and explain later. They're direct about feedback - both giving and receiving it - because they care more about getting things right than being polite.
They maintain high standards while moving at startup speed, and they build real relationships with teammates because they know that's how great work gets done. When things get tough, they adapt and keep pushing forward.
Our approach to AI
The people who thrive here treat AI like a natural extension of themselves. They've built their own ecosystem of agents - some for research, others for debugging, writing, analysis, or writing code. They know which AI works best for what problem.
Everyone gets premium accounts (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity Pro, Cursor, Lovable) plus a quarterly budget for new tools. But the magic happens in how we share knowledge. Demo days where someone shows off a clever workflows. Slack threads about which model handles a specific use case better. Learning from each other's AI workflows.
At Siena, we're not just looking for people who can do a job. We're looking for people who want to break boundaries, create the future, and reshape industries. If that's you, we look forward to your application.

GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

As an Intermediate Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you'll help developers find and fix security issues in their code by contributing to the static analysis engine that finds them.

Your work spans both the engine and the tools we use to evaluate it. You'll extend how the engine models programs, from parsing source code and resolving symbols to building call graphs and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You'll also build and apply tooling to test its findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, measuring both false positives and missed vulnerabilities.

We build the engine with artificial intelligence (AI) agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. You'll implement component specifications within the team's architecture, working with engineers and AI agents. Good judgment about when to trust agent output, and when to bring it to human review, is central to the role.

What you'll do

  • Extend the program model, including parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis, to support new languages and frameworks.
  • Build and apply AI-assisted tooling to implement, review, and validate engine changes and findings, in collaboration with the team's technical leadership. Measure detection quality against known vulnerabilities, judging changes primarily on false positive and false negative rates.
  • Develop static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) and the Open Worldwide Application Security Project (OWASP), along with test fixtures that demonstrate they work.
  • Implement component specifications with engineers and AI agents through phased plans and small, reviewable changes. Keep specifications and code in sync.
  • Improve the harness, agent instructions, and skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy. Use separate coding and reviewing agents, performance checks, application programming interface (API) checks, and dependency checks, and escalate risky changes to human review.
  • Solve technical problems of moderate scope and complexity, and identify and address technical debt that slows the team down.
  • Write maintainable code that meets our internal standards, and help maintain those standards through code review.
  • Participate in on-call rotations to help troubleshoot product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues.
  • Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.

What you'll bring

  • Experience using AI or large language model (LLM) tools to generate or evaluate technical content, with the judgment to assess when their output is trustworthy.
  • Solid professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Rust or Go. Our engine is written in Rust, the analyzer wrapper in Go, and the monolith integration in Ruby. You'll be willing to work across them.
  • An interest in static analysis and application security, including parsing, intermediate representations, taint and data-flow analysis, and how vulnerabilities arise in code. Deep expertise isn't required; we'll help you grow it.
  • Organize and progress your work independently in a remote, largely asynchronous environment.
  • The ability to communicate technical problems clearly and concisely and propose iterative solutions.
  • Helpful but not required: experience with performance optimization, Docker and continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), web or mobile frameworks, guardrails for agent-written code such as mutation testing and fuzzing, or program analysis and security research through publications or open source contributions. Willingness to learn performance optimization and containerized workflows is also welcome.

About the team

The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories. We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules and flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.

At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world.

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund

About ElevenLabs
ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.
We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $22B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:
• 
ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.
• 
ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.
• 
ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.
Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work
• 
High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.
• 
Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.
• 
AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.
• 
Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.
• 
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer
• 
Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
• 
Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.
• 
Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.
• 
Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.
• 
Annual team offsite: Each year, we bring your entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia, Italy and Cancún
• 
Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.
About the role
We're scaling from 1,000 → 4,000 employees across 50+ countries, and the complexity of how we support our people through performance, conflict, and change is growing quickly. Our Employee Relations (ER) Partners protect fairness, consistency, and trust as we grow. You'll own our most sensitive and complex People cases, so that leads can act early.
As an ER Partner at ElevenLabs, you'll lead formal performance processes, investigations, grievances, and disciplinary matters from start to finish, working closely with Legal and outside counsel across many jurisdictions. You'll also coach leads through difficult conversations before they become formal cases, and turn what you see into playbooks, frameworks, and training that reduce risk and case volume over time.
This is our first ER hire. We're building a dedicated ER function, and we want someone who can help shape and build it out: how cases are triaged and escalated, how we work with counsel, and how we measure what's working.
This is a high-impact role for someone who can handle sensitive situations with discretion, make sound judgment calls, and bring clarity and calm to fast-moving environments.

You will
• 
Lead formal performance processes, including back on track plans, end to end, in partnership with Leads and People Partners.
• 
Run fair, well-documented investigations into misconduct allegations, grievances, and complaints, from fact-finding through to outcome.
• 
Manage disciplinary, dismissal, and exit matters, drafting outcomes and communications with Legal.
• 
Partner with in-house employment counsel and, when necessary, outside counsel to assess risk.
• 
Triage incoming cases with People Partners using clear escalation criteria, so the right cases reach ER at the right time.
• 
Keep the case log and report on patterns, risks, and trends by team, region, and case type.
• 
Build playbooks, templates, and training that raise lead capability and cut avoidable cases.
• 
Build out a self-serve ER flow for leads, so that common ER cases become scalable.
• 
Partner with People Ops & Compliance teams to ensure smooth execution of terminations, local requirements, and compliance-heavy workflows.
Requirements
• 
Hands-on experience leading employee relations cases, including performance management, investigations, grievances, and disciplinaries, ideally in a fast-growing company.
• 
Strong judgment and the ability to handle sensitive issues with discretion, clarity, and fairness.
• 
Solid working knowledge of employment law principles and comfort working alongside in-house and outside counsel.
• 
Skilled in writing clear, defensible documentation and coaching leads through hard conversations.
• 
Comfortable moving fast and staying agile, shifting priorities quickly as cases and the business change, without losing rigour.
• 
Comfortable building process as well as running cases, as the ER function is still being built.
• 
Experience supporting globally distributed teams or multi-jurisdiction environments is a strong plus.
Location
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in on the East Coast USA or Europe.

About Carrot: 

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com.
The Opportunity 

Carrot is looking for a Director, Information Security to lead the security program that protects the highly sensitive fertility and family-building data of members around the world. You will set the security strategy, own both corporate security (GRC, incident response, security awareness, vendor risk) and product security (application, cloud and infrastructure security, secure development lifecycle), and serve as the trusted voice on Carrot's security posture with executives, auditors, and enterprise customers.

Day to day, you will balance setting direction with staying close to the work: prioritizing risk with Engineering and IT, guiding audit and certification cycles, coaching a small and talented team, and joining customer conversations where security is part of the buying decision. Carrot has already earned SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, HITRUST, and PCI DSS compliance, so this role is about taking a strong foundation to the next level of maturity, not starting from scratch.

What makes this role different is the combination of stakes and influence. Few security leaders get to protect data this personal, at global scale, while working directly with executive leadership and shaping how a health platform is built, sold, and trusted.

What You’ll Own 

In this role, you will:

• Lead Carrot's security strategy and roadmap, using a recognized maturity model (such as C2M2 or NIST CSF) to prioritize investments and report progress to executive leadership

• Own the full security program across corporate security (GRC, incident management, security awareness, third-party risk) and product security (application security, cloud and infrastructure security, secure SDLC)

• Partner with Engineering, especially the Internal Platform team, to build security into how Carrot designs, ships, and operates its systems, going beyond compliance

• Lead internal risk assessments across application, cloud, and corporate environments and turn the results into prioritized technical safeguards

• Own the compliance portfolio, including SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and HIPAA, and prepare Carrot for additional frameworks such as ISO 27001 as the business requires

• Direct incident response readiness, including playbooks, tabletop exercises, executive communication, and post-incident learning

• Represent Carrot's security posture to employers, health plans, and health systems through security reviews, questionnaires, and strategic sales conversations

• Work with Legal and Privacy to meet global data protection requirements (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA/CPRA) for member health data

• Build, coach, and grow the security team, balancing hands-on execution with delegation as the team scales

• Manage the security budget, tooling, and vendor relationships, and tailor security guidance for a remote-first workforce and physical offices

What Success Looks Like  

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

• A documented, executive-endorsed security strategy and multi-year roadmap with clear priorities, owners, and measures of progress

• Clean outcomes on recurring audits and certifications (SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS), with remediation items closed on schedule

• A tested incident response program, with regular tabletop exercises completed and lessons learned built back into the program

• A measurable reduction in high-risk vulnerabilities and open security findings, with remediation timelines agreed on with Engineering

• A living risk register and vendor security review process that leaders rely on to make decisions

• A security team with defined roles, clear growth paths, and the right capacity for Carrot's growth, including key hires made

• Faster, more consistent security reviews for Sales and Customer Success, with fewer escalations from enterprise customers

• A clear plan, and visible progress, on any additional frameworks the business prioritizes, such as ISO 27001

About You 

You likely have:

• A bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent experience)

• 10+ years of experience in technology, including 5+ years in information security and at least 3 years leading security teams

• A security certification such as CISSP or CISM

• Experience leading the security function at a late-stage startup, scale-up, or public company

• Working depth in healthcare data protection and privacy frameworks, including HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA/CPRA

• Experience overseeing enterprise frameworks and audits such as SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001

• Strong knowledge of application, network, and cloud security (AWS and Azure) and frameworks such as NIST CSF and OWASP

• Experience running core security programs, including incident response, risk management, vulnerability management, penetration testing, and security awareness

• Executive-level communication skills and confidence engaging customers and sales teams on security requirements

• Experience managing budget and allocating resources across people, tools, and vendors

Nice to Have ⭐

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

• Experience leading security through a major company event such as an IPO, acquisition, or large-scale audit cycle

• A background in healthcare, digital health, or another highly regulated, high-trust environment

• Experience leading security in a remote-first, globally distributed company

• Familiarity with compliance automation platforms such as Drata

• Experience building a security engineering practice alongside platform and infrastructure teams

Why This Role Matters 

Members trust Carrot with some of the most personal information a person can share, often during some of the most meaningful moments of their lives. Protecting that trust is not a back-office function. It is what allows employers, health plans, and health systems to bring Carrot to millions of people worldwide.

As Carrot grows, security leadership shapes how we build, how we sell, and how we show up for customers. In this role, you will make security a strength that members and customers can see and rely on, and build a team that keeps raising the bar as the business scales.
